outcome: Enterprise evaluation, student self/enterprise/position evaluation, advisor evaluation, server-fact score compute, independent review, final publish, version-bound appeal, withdrawal and recompute now form one continuous 4+1 product flow. Old-placement enterprise evaluations cannot complete or score a new placement; clients cannot forge five score components; reviewed scores cannot bypass the audited return command; independent score archive has been removed from the product surface and corrected in verified help knowledge.
invariants: Every enterprise evaluation freezes placementSnapshotId, enterpriseId and positionId from the exact current formal placement; current-task queries and score sources match all three fields.
A placement change preserves the old evaluation as historical evidence but creates a new evaluation task and rejects resubmit/review of the old placement as current truth.

School score readiness requires one SUBMITTED and APPROVED student evaluation with student enterprise/position ratings and a non-null advisor opinion; missing evaluation-chain facts leave the score incomplete.

The effective score compute command rejects checkinScore, weeklyScore, monthlyScore, enterpriseScore and schoolScore from clients. It derives suggested scores from authoritative process/evaluation facts; manual deltas require a reason and canonical evidence files.
A score moves PENDING_REVIEW to PENDING_PUBLISH through a distinct versioned review command, then PENDING_PUBLISH to PUBLISHED through a distinct final publish command.
A PENDING_PUBLISH score cannot be recomputed directly; it must first use the reasoned, versioned RETURN_RECALC command so the transition is explicit and audited.
Manual adjustment reviewer and adjuster use stable user IDs and must be different users; publish rechecks the review, source hash, evidence snapshots and ASSESS compliance.
Review, publish, withdraw and appeal decisions fail closed when the high-risk audit outbox is unhealthy, while domain trail facts are committed in the same database transaction.

A student appeal is a dedicated domain-bound work order that freezes scoreId and scoreVersion. Acceptance compares that exact published version, atomically withdraws it, and requires recompute, review and republish.
The tenant plus internship unique constraint permits only one FinalScore record; historical versions remain on that record and in immutable compute/audit snapshots.

Staff exposes missing, pending-calculate, pending-review, pending-publish and appeal queues with source-readiness indicators and persistent receipts; Student PC, both Mini surfaces and Enterprise Portal retain their server IDs and versions.
Scores have no independent archive action. The total internship archive is the only authority that freezes a published score and its source snapshot into the final Manifest.
